_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). THE RICHEST TILE IN THE SUMMIT BAND, and the only one in this set that is not almost pure stone. It is the left edge of the scroll at the bottom of the summit band, where the distant peaks come down to an inhabited shelf. Three distinct kinds of content, and they must not be masked the same way. (1) DISTANT TREE LINES along the peak crests, upper half: small trees drawn as a dark vertical trunk stroke under a flat horizontally-spreading dotted crown, strung in files along every ridge silhouette -- across the top edge, down the left slope, along the diagonal crest through the centre, crowning the second peak at x 0.50-0.63, and in a dense band across the upper right. These are pure ink, no colour, and individually tiny; they are catalogued as bands, not as trees. (2) A NEAR GROVE AND A SETTLEMENT in the lower right quadrant, x 0.56-1.0, y 0.55-1.0: tall slender trees with warm ochre trunks and dense blue-green dotted foliage, standing around a thatched-roof hall and a second smaller building, with a seated figure at the foot of the grove. This is the only place in the tile with leaf COLOUR and the only foliage with enough size to carry real motion. (3) A STAND OF TALL PINES clipped by the bottom-left corner, x 0.00-0.24, y 0.72-1.0, drawn in dark ink with straight trunks and layered needle whorls, no colour at all. THE DECOYS. The worst is the dark vertical band at x 0.54-0.70, y 0.15-0.58: a shadowed cliff edge carrying an almost continuous curtain of 点苔 moss dabs, the densest dark mass in the tile and the first thing any darkness or saturation threshold will grab. Magnified it has no trunks, no crowns, and the dabs stream DOWNHILL along the rock fold instead of standing upright -- it is stone. Second, the great pale face at x 0.22-0.60 below y 0.30 is combed with long parallel 牛毛皴 strokes that fan like needles at thumbnail size. Third, every ridge in the upper half carries moss along its silhouette immediately below the genuine tree files; the separating test in this tile is the vertical trunk stroke -- if the dark tuft has no stroke standing under it, it is moss on stone. Fourth, inside the settlement the thatched roofs are warm ochre, the same pigment family as the tree trunks, so a colour mask keyed on the trunks will animate the buildings; the architecture boxes below exist to be subtracted.

objects.name: tall blue-green trees left of the hall
objects.note: the largest genuine leaf mass in the tile: a stand of slender trees whose crowns are dense clusters of small dark leaf dots washed blue-green, on straight ochre trunks. Tops are ragged against bare silk at y~0.60, which makes this the cleanest silhouette in the tile and the best hinge subject. The trunks inside the box are wood and must be cut out by ink/ochre colour rather than by shrinking the box

objects.name: tree tops standing behind the hall roof
objects.note: the upper foliage of the grove, seen above and behind the thatched ridge line. The bottom edge of this box touches the roof -- hold it at y 0.68 or the roof enters the mask

objects.name: trees standing in front of and around the hall
objects.note: SEARCH REGION -- the hall's pale wall, its doorway and the stepped path are INSIDE this box, interleaved with the trunks. Perhaps half the pixels are architecture or ground. A per-pixel pass on the blue-green leaf dots is required; using this box as a mask would animate the building, which is the same class of error as animating the rock

objects.name: trees around the buildings, right edge
objects.note: SEARCH REGION for the same reason as grove-village-centre: the second thatched building and a fence sit inside it. Foliage here is the same blue-green dot clusters on ochre trunks, thinning toward the right edge where it continues into t009

objects.name: stand of tall pines, bottom left corner
objects.note: eight or ten tall pines with straight dark trunks and layered whorls of needles, clipped by the left and bottom edges. Pure ink with no wash of any kind, so a colour-keyed foliage pass misses them completely -- the opposite failure to the moss decoys. Their crowns stand against empty silk, so the silhouette is clean and they will hinge well

objects.name: tree file along the crest at the top edge
objects.note: SEARCH REGION. Small crowned trees standing on a crest that is clipped by the top edge; the ridge rock they stand on fills the lower part of the box. Continues upward into t004

objects.name: tree band down the central crest
objects.note: SEARCH REGION -- the trees run as a DIAGONAL band from upper-left to lower-right; the corners of the box are bare rock. The densest of the distant tree files, with individual trunks legible under the crowns at x 0.24-0.28

objects.name: tree band right of the central crest
objects.note: SEARCH REGION, continues ridge-trees-crest-diagonal down the saddle between the two peaks. Mixed with moss on the ridge below it; key on the tufts that stand clear of the silhouette

objects.name: trees crowning the second peak
objects.note: a compact group of flat-crowned trees standing on the flat top of the centre peak, with pale blue wash behind them. Small but unambiguous: trunks and crowns both legible. Directly ABOVE rock-cliff-dark-centre, the tile's worst decoy, so this pair is the one to check by eye if a mask looks wrong -- adjacent, similar in tone, opposite labels

objects.name: scattered trees down the left slope
objects.note: SEARCH REGION with a low fill fraction: half a dozen small trees scattered along a slope that falls to the lower left, most of the box being bare hemp-fibre rock between them. One patch of pale blue wash sits behind the trees near x 0.05, y 0.19

objects.name: dense tree line along the upper-right ridge
objects.note: SEARCH REGION. The heaviest of the distant tree files -- crowns crowded close enough to read as a continuous dark band, with trunks visible where the band thins at its left end. Runs along a crest that curves down to the right; the rock below the crest fills the bottom of the box. Continues into t009

objects.name: tree cluster on a ledge, right side
objects.note: a distinct clump of crowned trees on a projecting ledge, clipped by the right edge, with pale wash behind. Small but structurally clear

objects.name: pines on a rock spur, centre right
objects.note: a group of small pines standing on the nose of a spur, silhouetted against the pale misty gap behind them. Trunks are clearly drawn. Sits at the lower end of rock-cliff-dark-centre, so it is the first thing a mask will over-grab from -- keep the box tight to the crowns

objects.name: dark moss-curtained cliff edge, centre
objects.note: THE PRINCIPAL DECOY OF THIS TILE AND THE BAND. A long vertical band of dense 点苔 moss dabs laid down the shaded edge of the centre peak -- the darkest continuous mass in the tile, and at thumbnail size it looks exactly like a hanging wall of foliage. Magnified: no trunk anywhere, no crown, and the dabs stream downhill following the rock fold. If this box moves, the rock moves, which is precisely the defect that got the earlier automatic pass rejected

objects.name: the great pale cliff face, centre and lower centre
objects.note: the largest rigid region in the tile: a bare rounded rock mass combed with long parallel 牛毛皴 strokes that fan downhill and mimic needle sprays at small scale. No leaf glyph anywhere in it. NEVER animate

objects.name: ridge body under the left tree lines
objects.note: the stone the top-edge and left-slope tree files stand on, moss-dotted along its silhouette. That edge moss is the small-scale version of rock-cliff-dark-centre and is the reason those tree boxes must stay search regions

objects.name: long rock slope, left and lower left
objects.note: pale combed slope falling to the pines in the bottom corner. Rigid

objects.name: cliff below the upper-right tree line
objects.note: hemp-fibre cliff carrying the upper-right ridge; its moss chains sit immediately under the genuine tree band above and must be excluded from it

objects.name: rock shoulder above the settlement, right
objects.note: the stone shelf the settlement grove is planted on. Rigid

objects.name: main thatched-roof hall
objects.note: a broad thatched roof in warm ochre wash with combed straw strokes and a ruled ridge beam. RIGID, and it must be SUBTRACTED from grove-village-behind-hall and grove-village-centre, which overlap it -- its ochre is the same pigment as the tree trunks, so a colour mask keyed on trunks will take the roof with it

objects.name: hall wall, doorway and courtyard below the roof
objects.note: pale wall with a ruled doorway and a fenced court, drawn in fine dark line with no wash, seen between the trunks of the grove. Rigid; subtract from grove-village-centre

objects.name: second thatched building, lower right
objects.note: a smaller ochre thatched structure clipped by the right edge, continuing into t009. Rigid; subtract from grove-village-right

objects.name: seated figure at the foot of the grove
objects.note: a robed figure in fine 白描 outline with a pale unwashed robe, seated on the path at the bottom edge, clipped. BELOW THE SIZE FLOOR and registered as a landmark only, not as an animation target -- it is recorded because it is the human anchor of this settlement and because anything moving nearby must not drag it

objects.name: pale misty gap behind the right spur
objects.note: an area of almost untouched silk between the centre cliff and the right shoulder, reading as depth/mist and giving spur-trees-right-mid its clean silhouette. No strokes to animate; recorded so a mask does not treat the abrupt tonal edge around it as an object boundary
